newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent marked lower as NYMEX edges down.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent marked lower as NYMEX edges down.

text.p: September Brent crude futures were marked lower by midday in Asia on Friday, tracking moderate retracement on NYMEX following overnight gains.
Crude futures rose in London and New York overnight as MTBE tightness and a tropical storm boost gasoline prices.
However, short-term profits were taken on ACCESS trade to cut back NYMNEX crude gains, brokers said. Otherwise, markets appeared supported, they said.
September Brent on SIMEX was untraded at midday but quoted at $18.50/$18.68 per barrel, down from London's settlement price of $18.69, which marked a 39-cent gain on the day.
August NYMEX crude was last traded at $19.93 per barrel, down six cents from the New York NYMEX close of $19.99.
New York values rose 34 cents off the back of a strong gasoline market.
Tropical Storm Danny was brewing in the U.S. Gulf, prompting worries that it could affect refinery operations and deliveries.
In addition, MTBE prices have risen sharply in recent days prompting a build up of long positions in the gasoline contract.
MTBE is a blending component in the reformulated gasoline grade deliverable against the gasoline contract.
August gasoline on ACCESS was last traded at 61.95 cents per gallon, up 0.06 from New York, where the contract rose 1.43.
